description: Named after the theoretical tachyon, a particle that challenges conventional boundaries, our mission is to push beyond the ordinary. For this challenge, we aim to combine physics, computational science, AI, and scientific data analysis to explore microgravity combustion and uncover insights that can contribute to safer human space exploration. We believe the best ideas emerge where different disciplines collide.
summary:
FlameBound is an educational prototype for exploring how atmospheric conditions relate to fire research in space. Users can ask scientific questions, look up information in locally indexed NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) project files, calculate oxygen partial pressure, and compare two gas atmospheres. Atmospheric calculations are performed deterministically by the backend; the AI assistant explains results and can cite retrieved PSI passages, which are clearly labeled unreviewed.

The project addresses the challenge of making spaceflight fire research easier to explore and understand. Oxygen concentration and total pressure both affect an atmosphere, while microgravity changes how flames behave. FlameBound brings these topics together in a web interface that connects a React frontend, a FastAPI scientific backend, and a local Ollama assistant. It is a research and education prototype: it does not predict flame spread, certify fire safety, or claim that its locally retrieved source passages have been scientifically reviewed.
details:
FlameBound is a web prototype for exploring how atmospheric conditions relate to fire research in space. Users can ask general science questions, calculate oxygen partial pressure from an oxygen fraction and absolute pressure, compare two atmospheres, and search NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) files related to BASS and SAFFIRE experiments.

The calculation engine runs deterministically in the Python/FastAPI backend. A local Ollama language model handles conversational explanations, while a local text retriever searches PSI files and attaches citations. Retrieved passages are labeled unreviewed. The project does not predict flame spread, certify fire safety, or provide operational safety decisions.

FlameBound aims to make spaceflight fire research easier to explore and explain, while showing the difference between a calculation, general background, and information found in source files. We considered scientific traceability, missing or unclear inputs, uncertainty, data provenance, and the risk of AI-generated claims. Local PSI retrieval covers only files with extractable text; some scans and a sensitive workbook are excluded.

We used Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, React, JavaScript, Vite, Ollama, and NASA PSI data. ChatGPT/Codex assisted with code, documentation, and debugging; Ollama generates conversational explanations in the app. No AI-generated images, video, or audio were used. NASA data itself was not AI-generated.
